item.title: Vibe Coding Is Dead, Long Live Agentic Engineering
item.description: Six months ago “vibe coding” meant typing a vague prompt and hoping the output compiled. I did it. It worked until it didn’t — the moment a codebase got past toy-project size, prompt-and-hope fell apart. What replaced it, quietly, wasn’t a better prompt. It was a different job description. The shift nobody announced I still write code every day. I just don’t type most of it anymore. The work moved up a level: instead of implementing a function, I write a spec for what the function needs to do, constraints it has to respect, and then I watch an agent build it.
